item.text: {"rubric":[{"claim_id":"C1","claim_type":"core","weight":35,"statement":"The program builds an LM from a bare model ID such as `gpt-4o-mini`, patches `litellm.get_supported_openai_params` and `litellm.supports_response_schema`, and asserts both mocks were called with `custom_llm_provider == \"openai\"`, demonstrating that DSPy treats slashless model names as OpenAI for capability probing.","span_ids":["E1"]},{"claim_id":"C2","claim_type":"supporting","weight":20,"statement":"The program patches `litellm.completion` and shows the mocked JSON payload can pass through the structured-output call path under `dspy.JSONAdapter`, for example by asserting `prediction.answer == \"ok\"`.","span_ids":["E4","E5"]},{"claim_id":"C3","claim_type":"core","weight":25,"statement":"The program prints or asserts that `lm.provider` is the base `Provider` rather than `OpenAIProvider`, showing that LM construction used the generic fallback from `infer_provider()` instead of binding the bare model to an OpenAI provider object.","span_ids":["E2","E3"]},{"claim_id":"C4","claim_type":"core","weight":20,"statement":"The program calls `lm.finetune(train_data=[], train_data_format=None)` and asserts it raises `ValueError` with the unsupported-fine-tuning message (for example containing `does not support fine-tuning`), proving fine-tuning is blocked even though capability probing used `openai`.","span_ids":["E6"]}],"evidence":[{"span_id":"E1","path":"dspy/clients/lm.py","start_line":115,"end_line":137},{"span_id":"E2","path":"dspy/clients/lm.py","start_line":74,"end_line":78},{"span_id":"E3","path":"dspy/clients/lm.py","start_line":307,"end_line":310},{"span_id":"E4","path":"dspy/clients/lm.py","start_line":159,"end_line":198},{"span_id":"E5","path":"dspy/clients/lm.py","start_line":385,"end_line":398},{"span_id":"E6","path":"dspy/clients/lm.py","start_line":247,"end_line":260}]}
